findings.text: When a page or folio feature is compiled out, its generated helpers become inert: test style helpers report absent or zero and set or clear style helpers leave state unchanged. This covers the FALSE and NOOP macro families for page and folio flags.

Availability of several flags is configuration dependent. Swap cache, lock state, poison, idle and young tracking, reported accounting and self hosted vmemmap each have an active form under one configuration and a false or no-op form otherwise, with 64 bit further gating young and idle.
Low pointer bits distinguish anonymous mappings: anon alone is 1, anon KSM is 2, combined KSM is both bits, and the mask covering both is their union.

Anonymous status is derived from low mapping pointer bits. Lazy free means anonymous without swap backing. One predicate requires exactly the anonymous bit without KSM, another requires both bits for merged KSM, and slab pages must be excluded before using the anonymous test because slab reuses the same storage.

Uptodate has paired ordering. The test only orders subsequent data reads after observing the flag set. Both marking paths order prior data stores before publishing the flag, with atomic and non-atomic variants, and page wrappers forward to the folio implementation.

Large folio is equivalent to head folio. Head state is testable on both folio and page, with non-atomic set and both atomic and non-atomic clear forms. Clearing compound state is only valid on a head page and results in clearing head.

Head mask is one shifted by the head bit position. Poison mask is one shifted by the poison bit when memory failure is enabled else zero. Locked mask is one shifted by the locked bit when enabled else zero.

Page type codes reserve low values for map counts and high values for types: buddy F0, offline F1, table F2, guard F3, hugetlb F4, slab F5, zsmalloc F6, unaccepted F7, large kmalloc F8, and mapcount underflow FF.

Type is stored in the top byte of the page type word, with all bits set meaning no type. Helpers detect typed versus count values, including an off by one mapcount check, and generated set and clear operations enforce single ownership with debug checks and early return on idempotent transitions.

Concrete typed pages provided are table, guard, slab, hugetlb, zsmalloc, unaccepted and large kmalloc, with hugetlb reduced to a false test when disabled. Huge status for a page is determined through its folio hugetlb state.

Hardware poison containment checks both direct and indirect state: a page counts as poisoned if itself flagged or if it belongs to a hugetlb folio whose head is flagged; a folio counts as containing poison if itself flagged or if large and marked as having a poisoned member.

Exclusive anonymous state lives on the head for hugetlb and per page for THP. Setting or clearing requires non KSM anonymous state and head position for hugetlb, while the unlocked clear accepts broader anonymous state. Movable operations are only present when the movable flag is set together with offline or zsmalloc state.

Free time, preparation time, second word and private flag combinations define expected or forbidden bit sets. Free checks core LRU and lock related bits plus locked and generation masks. Prep checks the general mask without poison plus generation and reference masks. Second covers order plus poison and mapping shape bits. Private covers the two private bits, and folio private presence is a nonzero test of that pair.
Reported free page test and set use non-atomic access and rely on external zone lock protection. Unaccepted page marking is likewise serialized by the zone lock.
Block statistics keep per direction counters for time, sectors, completed operations and merges, plus a shared tick counter and two in flight counters using local counters.

Parman priority management uses an item with list linkage and position, a priority bucket with list linkage plus its own item list and priority value, and an operations table carrying base size, growth step, resize and move callbacks and algorithm choice. Only list sort algorithm is defined.

Taint descriptor carries set and unset display characters plus a description. Option matcher pairs a numeric token with a pattern string and defines an array table type. Substring is a from and to pointer pair. P2P DMA provider pairs an owner device with a bus offset.
Taint positions run 0 through 19 from proprietary module to fwctl, with count 20 and maximum mask of all low 20 bits set. Invalid panic CPU is negative one. Maximum option arguments is 3.
Architecture panic timeout update is conditional: it replaces the global timeout only when the global still equals the supplied architecture default.

Isolation queries have enabled and disabled shapes. When enabled, page and type isolation test for the isolate migrate type and block isolation manipulates a per block bit. When disabled, all tests report false and setters do nothing.

Isolation reasons are memory offline, contiguous allocation, and other. Lock dependency health is either still reliable or now unreliable. P2P DMA mapping outcomes distinguish unknown, none, unsupported bridge traversal, direct bus address use, and allowed bridge traversal with normal addressing.
Partition statistics short critical sections disable and re-enable preemption around per CPU access rather than taking a spin lock.

Partition counters are per CPU and aggregated by summing over all possible CPUs. Initialization writes a uniform byte value across every CPU record. Additive updates use this CPU addition and propagate partition updates to the whole device. Decrement, increment and subtract are expressed through addition, while local operations use local counter primitives on the current CPU view.

Clearing compound state faults when invoked on a non head page. Exclusive anonymous accessors enforce debug preconditions on anonymous, KSM and head placement. Waiter detection combines a caller mask with current folio flags through a negative byte test.
